title: Salience Labs Wants To Scale Up AI With Silicon Photonics Optical Switch
gist: Oxford/Munster spinout Salience Labs is shipping a 32-port all-silicon-photonics optical circuit switch (OC-32M) with under 10 nanoseconds port-to-port latency - roughly 25X lower than Broadcom's Tomahawk Ultra Ethernet ASIC at about 250 nanoseconds - and under 300 microsecond reconfiguration versus milliseconds for MEMS. The pitch is to break the 72-GPU scale-up ceiling shared by Nvidia and AMD rackscale designs; Salience Labs models an 80 percent gain in tokens per second per user on a hypothetical 576-GPU cluster running Nvidia's Megatron 2T.

insights.claim: The port-to-port hop on Salience Labs' shipping OC-32M optical circuit switch is under 10 nanoseconds, which the author calls main memory speed, versus around 250 nanoseconds for Broadcom's Tomahawk Ultra Ethernet ASIC - a 25X latency advantage.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: A 25X switch-latency gap is the kind of gap that reshapes scale-up architecture; it is the core technical claim to verify.
insights.quote: The port to port hop on the initial OC-32M device that Salience Labs is now shipping is under 10 nanoseconds
insights.locator: The port to port hop on the initial OC-32M device

insights.claim: Other good Ethernet switches run 450 to 650 nanoseconds port to port and weaker ones reach milliseconds, which the author says makes them not appropriate for scale-up memory fabrics at all.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Sets the latency bar any Ethernet-based scale-up fabric proposal has to clear, and most do not.
insights.quote: Other Ethernet switches are on the order of 450 nanoseconds to 650 nanoseconds for very good ones, and can be milliseconds for ones that are really not appropriate for scale up memory fabrics at all.
insights.locator: Other Ethernet switches are on the order of 450 nanoseconds

insights.claim: On-chip waveguide switching reconfigures a port-to-port link in under 300 microseconds versus milliseconds for MEMS mirror and liquid crystal on silicon approaches, and Salience Labs claims a reconfiguration-time advantage of more than 3X over MEMS.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Reconfiguration speed determines whether an OCS can be used dynamically inside a job rather than only between jobs - the difference between a niche and a platform.
insights.locator: What matters is that it is not mirrors or LCDs

insights.claim: Energy consumption per port is 8X lower for either type of optical circuit switch compared with a relatively fast Ethernet switch.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Power per port is becoming a binding datacenter constraint; an 8X networking power reduction is a material capex and opex argument.
insights.quote: The energy consumption per port is 8X lower for either type of OCS compared to a relatively fast Ethernet switch
insights.locator: The key thing to notice is how that reconfiguration time

insights.claim: The OC-32M outputs 100 Gb/sec native line rate with PAM4 modulation carrying two bits per signal to reach 200 Gb/sec effective bandwidth per lane.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Per-lane bandwidth determines whether the OCS can keep up with HBM-class fabrics; 200 Gb/sec effective is the number to compare against NVLink generations.
insights.locator: The output from the OCS is 100 Gb/sec native line rate

insights.claim: The scale-up domain for AI systems is stuck at 72 GPUs from both Nvidia and AMD, and prospective customers are talking to Salience Labs specifically about expanding beyond that single-rack coherent memory limit.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: A hard architectural ceiling shared by both accelerator vendors is exactly the kind of constraint that creates a new component category.
insights.quote: expanding the size of the scale up domain for an AI system, which is stuck at 72 GPUs from both Nvidia and AMD right now
insights.locator: What the potential customers talking to Salience Labs seem to be keen on

insights.claim: Salience Labs models that lower OCS latency at the scale-up layer improves token per second per user throughput by 80 percent on a hypothetical 576-GPU machine running Nvidia's Megatron 2T model, without moving to a dual-system architecture.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: An 80 percent throughput uplift from networking alone would materially change inference cost per token - the key economic claim, and it is vendor-modeled rather than measured.
insights.quote: That lower latency of the OCS at the scale up layer improves token per second per user throughput by 80 percent without having to move to a dual-system architecture
insights.locator: Here is the cut and dry of the argument for adoption

insights.claim: The core adoption argument is that optical circuit switching removes the need to run two different kinds of compute engines to get low latency inference, letting operators scale up across multiple racks and boost throughput while staying on GPUs.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: If true, it undercuts the case for specialized low-latency inference silicon - a competitive threat to disaggregated prefill/decode hardware plays.
insights.locator: Here is the cut and dry of the argument for adoption

insights.claim: Customer interest splits three ways: extending the coherent memory domain beyond one rack, finding an alternative to existing rackscale coherent memory fabrics, and using OCS for the first network layer gluing machines together for the decode phase of generative AI.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Three distinct demand vectors mean the addressable market is broader than a single scale-up replacement thesis.
insights.locator: Some customers want to go beyond one rack

themes.theme: Salience Labs technology and supply chain

insights.claim: Salience Labs spun out of Oxford University and the University of Munster from teams led by Oxford applied nanomaterials professor Harish Bhaskaran and Munster experimental physics professor Wolfram Pernice, whose joint research effort was on phase change optoelectronics.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Provenance in phase-change optoelectronics is the strongest clue to the undisclosed switching mechanism and to the IP moat.
insights.locator: The startup spun out of Oxford University

insights.claim: Salience Labs will not disclose its switching mechanism but confirms it is neither MEMS nor LCoS, and its partnership with Tower Semiconductor for PH18DA integrated III-V lasers and TPS45PH low-loss silicon nitride waveguides suggests a phase change approach inside a silicon photonics framework.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Names Tower Semiconductor as the manufacturing partner - the supply-chain read-through if this category scales.
insights.locator: The fact that Salience Labs has partnered with Tower Semiconductor

insights.claim: The Salience Labs product is two chips mounted back to back on a PCB card - a fully integrated silicon photonics optical circuit switch plus an amplification and signal conditioning chip analogous to retimers and redrivers for copper circuits.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: The amplification chip, not the switch itself, is described as the crux of the stack - that is where the defensible IP sits.
insights.quote: The Salience Labs OCS is comprised of two chips.
insights.locator: The Salience Labs OCS is comprised of two chips

insights.claim: CEO Vaysh Kewada says integrating on chip inevitably incurs optical loss and that Salience Labs solved it with its own amplification component fabricated in arrays to meet bill-of-materials cost goals, calling that amplification chip one of a kind and the crux of the stack.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Optical loss is the historical reason silicon photonics OCS failed; the amplification solution is the make-or-break engineering claim.
insights.quote: This amplification chip is one of a kind, and the crux of the stack.
insights.locator: With OCS, you want to be able to produce the product

insights.claim: Salience Labs launched its 32-port OCS in March and is now ramping production, with the architecture designed to scale to 64, 128, and 256 ports and up to eight modules packageable into a single 1U chassis.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: The port-count roadmap determines whether the product can address multi-rack scale-up domains; 32 ports today is not yet sufficient for the headline use case.
insights.locator: The OCS that Salience Labs launched in March

insights.claim: Google has used its 'Palomar' MEMS devices as part of the 'Apollo' optical circuit switch as the backbone of its TPU clusters for the past four generations since 2015, allowing up to 9,216 TPUs to be lashed together in a coherent memory cluster and reconfigured on the fly.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Google already proved OCS works at AI scale - the strongest existence proof for the category and the benchmark competitors must match.
insights.locator: Google hardwired the first three generations of its TPU

insights.claim: Lumentum sells MEMS-based OCS gear and has aspirations beyond telecom in the AI datacenter, while Coherent sells liquid crystal on silicon OCS devices, and Nvidia has partnered with both companies for various optical technologies.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Nvidia has hedged across both incumbent OCS technologies, signaling it takes optical circuit switching seriously for future rackscale designs.
insights.locator: Lumentum, which has partnered with Nvidia

insights.claim: Salience Labs CEO Vaysh Kewada argues OCS is a market ripe for disruption because the optical circuit switches available today are based on technology that is fundamentally twenty years old if not older.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: A twenty-year-old technology base in a market suddenly pulled into AI scale-up is the classic setup for incumbent displacement.
insights.quote: Our view is OCS was a market ripe for disruption, because the OCSes that are available today on the market are based off a technology that fundamentally is twenty years old if not older.
insights.locator: But what was interesting to us was that this trend

insights.claim: Salience Labs' founding hypothesis was that as optical connections proliferate in the datacenter in any format - pluggable, CPO, NPO - the switching layers would move toward heterogeneous architectures combining electrical packet switches in some cases and optical circuit switches in others.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: A reusable model for how datacenter networking evolves: optics proliferation forces switch-layer heterogeneity rather than wholesale replacement.
insights.locator: We chose to develop OCS because our view is that

insights.claim: Optical circuit switches are not new and have been used in network research labs and telecom production for two and a half decades, so the novelty is their migration into the scale-up network domain of HPC and AI clusters rather than the technology itself.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Reframes OCS as a proven technology finding a new market - lower technical risk, higher timing risk, than a true greenfield bet.
insights.quote: Optical circuit switches are not new and have been used in network technology research labs and in the telecom industry in production for the past two and a half decades.
insights.locator: Optical circuit switches are not new

insights.claim: The author closes by directing the argument at the accelerator vendors themselves, signaling his view that OCS-based scale-up is a live architectural option Nvidia and AMD should adopt rather than a startup curiosity.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: An editorial endorsement from a well-sourced infrastructure analyst raises the odds this becomes an acquisition or design-win story.
insights.quote: I hope Nvidia and AMD are listening.
insights.locator: I hope Nvidia and AMD are listening
